records.name: Balanced Veterans Network
records.summary: A veteran-led community for veterans and their families, with peer support, education and wellness resources on topics such as the move out of military service and suicide prevention.
records.what_you_do: Join the free online community through the website or the app, and take part in the listed events, such as a Veterans Day event, two 5K runs and retreats.

schedule.text: Ten events are listed for October and November 2026, including a Veterans Day event on November 1, two 5K runs, a gravel bike race and several retreats. The events page gives no places.

cost.text: Membership and the listed events are free.

first_step.how: Click Join Today on the website, or download the group's app, to set up a free membership.
first_step.basis: Membership is free and open to veterans and their families, with a clear way to sign up. The site does not say what a typical event feels like.

records.notes: IRS list name: Balanced Veterans. The batch website, balancedveterans.com, does not resolve; it redirects to balancedveterans.org, which a public directory also lists as the group's site, so that domain is used. The events page lists events for October and November 2026 with no places or sign-up steps; the status rests on those listed events. The site does not name Philadelphia. The Philadelphia location comes from the IRS list and public directories, and two conflicting addresses appear there (120 S. 21st Street and 776 Hill Rd), so no street address is recorded. Peer support and suicide prevention are part of the work; support_group is left false, and the owner should decide whether this belongs in the support flow. Social media links appear on the site but were not captured.

records.name: Christian Mental Health Initiative
records.summary: A nonprofit that works with churches and Christian groups on mental health, with training for church and community leaders and a page of local and online help options.
records.what_you_do: Attend a training for church or community leaders, use the group's mental health resources page, or follow its newsletter for updates.

first_step.how: Subscribe to the newsletter on the group's website, or email the team to ask about a training for your church or group.
first_step.basis: The newsletter and contact email are open to anyone, but the site does not describe a training schedule or how individuals take part.

records.notes: No dated events, news or newsletter issues on the site. The 2026 copyright footer is not used as evidence. Photo captions name a workshop at Catalyst Church and a Family Affair event at Christ Community Church, with no dates or links, so they are not listed as leads. No denomination is given, so faith is left null. No phone number is published.

records.name: Developing Excellence
records.notes: IRS list name: Developing Excellence Inc. The batch website, http://www.developingexcellence.net, did not resolve (DNS error on the www and bare domains, retried once). No search was used here because both searches went to other groups. No summary written. The IRS list address is 701 E Cathedral Rd Ste 45, the same suite that appears for Echo Collective and Specialists of Schools. Next step: search the name with Philadelphia.

records.name: Echo Collective
records.summary: A collective that pairs political education with organizing, helping people make sense of the world and work toward change together.
records.what_you_do: Email the collective to ask about its gatherings and how to take part. Its calendar page listed no dated events when checked.

first_step.how: Email echocollective@proton.me and ask how to join the next gathering.
first_step.basis: The only public way in is an email, and the site does not say what a gathering looks like or who attends.

records.notes: The site does not name a city. The IRS list places it at 701 E Cathedral Rd Ste 45, Philadelphia 19128, the same suite used by Developing Excellence and Specialists of Schools. Confirm it serves Philadelphia before showing it. The site does not say whether the group is partisan. No party or candidate is named on the pages read, but check before publishing. The agenda page lists no events for October to December 2026. The collaborators page and the files page were not read.

records.name: Empowering Freedom
records.summary: A peer-led group based in Philadelphia that runs mental health trainings, such as the WRAP wellness planning course and Mental Health First Aid, and offers peer-led services.
records.what_you_do: Request a training through the form on the group's website, or join the mailing list to hear about upcoming trainings and events.

first_step.how: Fill in the Request a Training form on the group's website to ask about the next WRAP seminar or Mental Health First Aid course.
first_step.basis: Trainings are open to requests from the public through a form, but the site does not say what a training is like or how many people attend.

records.notes: Dated homepage items: Peerpocalypse 2026 (May 4 to 7, 2026, Seaside, Oregon) and a June 26 to 29, 2026 conference presentation in Kenya. Both are speaking events outside Philadelphia, so they show the group is active, not that it meets locally. The site has template leftovers (a placeholder account email, a Pay Here button and a training link that go nowhere, an undated gallery post), so confidence is low. Second phone number on the site: (302) 547-2607. The LinkedIn link on the site is labeled for a different organization and was not recorded. Counseling, group therapy and case management are listed as services; support_group is left false, and the owner should check that against the support flow rule. Legal form not stated.

records.name: Influencing Social Policy
records.notes: A national association for social work educators, students and practitioners. The site names no Philadelphia address, chapter, meeting or program. Its only dated item is the Macro United 2027 conference, hosted in Chicago. Membership runs through an online portal, and no fees appear on the page read. The IRS list gives a Philadelphia ZIP (19128), but that address is not published on the site and is not recorded here. Reconsider if a Philadelphia program turns up. Dropped lead: the Macro United conference site (macrounited.org) is a conference, not a group, so it was not fetched.

records.name: Limitless Ladies Ministries
records.summary: A Christ-centered nonprofit ministry for women. It runs Love Bags, care packages of everyday supplies and encouraging cards for people in need, plus teen workshops and life coaching.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a workshop from the events page, or help with Love Bags. The group asks people to get in touch to learn how to help.

schedule.text: Workshops and events are listed on the events page for spring and summer 2025, including teen workshops and a community event. No 2026 events are listed.

first_step.how: Check the events page for the next teen or community workshop and use its link to register, or call 302-468-7234 to ask about a workshop or about helping with Love Bags.
first_step.basis: Workshops have a posted sign-up link and the group invites people to get in touch, but the site does not say what a typical workshop involves.

records.notes: IRS list kind was congregation. The group describes itself as a nonprofit ministry that runs programs, so kind is nonprofit. Denomination not stated, so faith is null. The newest dated event is August 30, 2025, listed as Philadelphia with no venue. The newsletter sign-up notes it may not work yet. The email uses a different domain (limitlessladiesforever.org) from the website; recorded as published. The April 26, 2025 teen workshop is named on the events page as a Fathership Foundation program, with no link, so it is not listed as a lead.

records.name: Oaks of Hope International
records.summary: A nonprofit that gives devotionals, workshops, resources and donated goods to groups that support girls and women who have faced trafficking, abuse, addiction and hopelessness.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer as a Hope Pillar by writing blog posts, serving at virtual or live events, sponsoring a workshop, sharing a story, making art or facilitating a workshop.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer form on the group's volunteer page with your name, email and the areas you are interested in.
first_step.basis: The form is the only public way in, and the page does not say how volunteers are matched or what a first task looks like.

records.notes: The site does not name Philadelphia. The IRS list gives a Philadelphia ZIP (19128), so the city comes from there and needs confirming. The volunteer page shows a post timestamp of September 22, 2026 in its header; that is the newest dated sign of life used. The homepage timestamp of April 2025 and a December 2024 partner testimonial are older. The 2024 footer is not used. The page does not say whether volunteering is remote. A partner named in a testimonial (Rooted In Love Ministries) has no link, so it is not listed as a lead. The X link on the site is empty.

records.name: Save Cambodia
records.summary: A nonprofit advocacy group that aims to unite Cambodians around the world and push for accountability and reform in Cambodia, through volunteer reporting, campaigns and advocacy at the United Nations.
records.what_you_do: Join the community through the group's Join Now page, watch or attend its community briefings and discussions, and volunteer for reporting and campaign work.

schedule.text: Community briefings and discussions are listed on the group's calendar, usually on Saturday afternoons and often held online. The most recent listed briefing was in April 2026.

locations.label: Mailing address (PO box, no meetings published)

first_step.how: Join the community through the group's Join Now page, then watch for the next community briefing on its calendar.
first_step.basis: Briefings are announced on a public calendar and the community join page is open to anyone, but the site does not describe a volunteer onboarding.

records.notes: Newest dated items: urgent action pages dated August 7 and August 14, 2026 on the homepage. The calendar lists community briefings on January 3 and April 25, 2026. The footer year is 2025 and is not used. Track record items are dated by year only. The calendar gives a street address (4431 Main Street, Philadelphia 19127) as the place for some briefings; it is not recorded because most events are online and the site gives a mailbox. The owner may decide whether to show it. The newsletter sign-up notes it may not work as published. The member login was not used. The Commission of Inquiry for Cambodia (cambodiacommissionofinquiry.org) is a project this group sponsors, not a separate group, so it was dropped as a lead after a check. Its advocacy concerns the Cambodian government and human rights, not a U.S. party or campaign, so it is in scope.

records.name: Specialists of Schools
records.summary: A membership network for Philadelphia-area professionals whose work involves students. Members network, learn about local services for students and take part in continuing education.
records.what_you_do: Apply for membership, then join the networking events and continuing education workshops the group offers to members.

first_step.how: Use the Apply for Membership page on the group's website, or email admin@specialistsofschools.org, to ask about joining.
first_step.basis: Membership needs an application before you can see the events, and the events list was empty when checked.

records.notes: The site says it has over 300 members. The events page and the homepage show no dated events or news; the 2025 copyright footer is not used. The mailing address is a building mailbox, and the same street suite appears in the IRS list for Developing Excellence and Echo Collective. Not checked: the parents section (How SOS Can Help) and the FAQ.

records.name: Springboard Meditation Sangha
records.summary: A meditation community rooted in Buddhist practice, open to anyone who wants to practice together. It offers free online sessions and in-person gatherings in Philadelphia and nearby.
records.what_you_do: Join a free online sit or discussion on the group's schedule, or attend an in-person gathering, such as a morning session or a residential retreat.

schedule.text: Online meditation sessions and discussion groups are on a calendar the site links. Six in-person gatherings are listed for August to December 2026, mostly at Philadelphia venues, plus a residential retreat outside the city.

locations.label: Unitarian Society of Germantown, Sullivan Chapel (in-person gatherings)

cost.text: Online offerings are free and open to the public. The site gives no fee for in-person gatherings.

first_step.how: Use the Zoom link on the group's schedule page to join an online session, or email info@springboardsangha.org to ask about an in-person gathering.
first_step.basis: Online sessions are open to the public and the site has a page describing each practice, but it does not say beginners are specially welcome.

records.notes: IRS list kind was congregation. Kept as congregation because it is a religious sangha, though the site calls itself a meditation community and says it is nondenominational. Faith is set to buddhist because the site says it is oriented to Buddhist practitioners. The site says it was incorporated in 2011 as a lay nonprofit Buddhist organization. The site's mailing address is c/o an individual organizer, so only the ZIP (19129) is noted here and no street address is recorded. Teacher names are left out. The online calendar did not load on the schedule page, so online session times are not listed. Venue addresses are public venues.

records.notes: IRS list name: Bethel Agape Ministries Inc. The batch website field holds a name, not a web address, so no site was fetched. As a congregation it should not be rejected; confirm whether it holds public services before publishing.

records.notes: The batch website field holds the group's name, not a web address, so no site was fetched. No search was used, because both searches went to High Flock Comics and Balanced Veterans. A later run should search the name with Philadelphia. No summary written.

records.notes: The batch website field holds 'Precious Jewels Prevention Program LLC', a company name, not a web address, so no site was fetched. That may mean this entry is a prevention business rather than a group; check before publishing. No search was used. No summary written.

records.name: High Flock Comics

One search for 'High Flock Comics' Philadelphia found no shop, club or group by that name; the results were general guides to Philadelphia comic shops. The name may be spelled differently, or the group may be new or closed. No summary written. Next step: try name variants.

notes: Batch of 15 IRS-list groups. Search budget used in full (2 of 2): High Flock Comics (no match) and Balanced Veterans (the search showed its domain, which was then fetched). Fetch budget: 28 used of 60. Five groups are unknown records because they have no usable web address and were not searched: Bethel Agape Ministries, Cross Cultural Connect, Folamis Oasis, and Developing Excellence (its batch domain does not resolve; DNS failed on every try). High Flock Comics was searched but not found. A later run should search the four unsearched groups first. Dead or moved domains: balancedveterans.com redirects to balancedveterans.org; developingexcellence.net does not resolve. Dropped as leads: the Commission of Inquiry for Cambodia (a Save Cambodia project, not a separate group) and the Macro United conference (a conference, not a group). Named without links, so not listed as leads: Catalyst Church, Christ Community Church, Fathership Foundation, Rooted In Love Ministries, and the United Cambodian Association of Minnesota (not Philadelphia). No 403s, bot checks or logins were met. No forms were submitted and no one was contacted. Owner decisions to review: (1) Balanced Veterans and Empowering Freedom do peer support or suicide-prevention work, and support_group is false on both; the support flow rule may apply. (2) Echo Collective: its partisan status and Philadelphia location are both unconfirmed. (3) Oaks of Hope International: Philadelphia comes only from the IRS list. (4) Save Cambodia's calendar gives a Philadelphia street address for some briefings; not recorded. (5) Springboard's mailing address is c/o an individual, so only its ZIP is noted. Verdict counts: publish 14 (9 with content, 5 unknown and held back), out_of_area 1.
